{{Short description|Special mathematical function}}
{{About|the Dirichlet beta function|other beta functions|Beta function (disambiguation)}}
[[Image:Mplwp dirichlet beta.svg|thumb|right|325px|The Dirichlet beta function]]
In [[mathematics]], the '''Dirichlet beta function''' (also known as the '''Catalan beta function''') is a [[special function]], closely related to the [[Riemann zeta function]]. It is a particular [[Dirichlet L-function]], the L-function for the alternating [[Dirichlet character|character]] of period four.

==Definition==
The Dirichlet beta function is defined as

:<math>\beta(s) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n} {(2n+1)^s},</math>

or, equivalently,

:<math>\beta(s) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(s)}\int_0^{\infty}\frac{x^{s-1}e^{-x}}{1 + e^{-2x}}\,dx.</math>

In each case, it is assumed that Re(''s'')&nbsp;>&nbsp;0.

Alternatively, the following definition, in terms of the [[Hurwitz zeta function]], is valid in the whole complex ''s''-plane:<ref>[http://engineeringandmathematics.blogspot.co.nz/2012/09/dirichlet-beta-hurwitz-zeta-relation.html Dirichlet Beta – Hurwitz zeta relation], Engineering Mathematics</ref>

:<math>\beta(s) = 4^{-s} \left( \zeta\left(s,{1 \over 4}\right)-\zeta\left( s, {3 \over 4}\right) \right).</math>

Another equivalent definition, in terms of the [[Lerch transcendent]], is:

:<math>\beta(s) = 2^{-s} \Phi\left(-1,s,{{1} \over {2}}\right),</math>

which is once again valid for all complex values of ''s''.

The Dirichlet beta function can also be written in terms of the [[polylogarithm]] function:

:<math>\beta(s) = \frac{i}{2} \left(\text{Li}_s(-i)-\text{Li}_s(i)\right).</math>

Also the series representation of Dirichlet beta function can be formed in terms of the [[polygamma function]]

:<math>\beta(s) =\frac{1}{2^s} \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^{n}}{\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{s}}=\frac1{(-4)^s(s-1)!}\left[\psi^{(s-1)}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)-\psi^{(s-1)}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\right] </math>

but this formula is only valid at positive integer values of <math>s</math>.

== Euler product formula ==

It is also the simplest example of a series non-directly related to <math>\zeta(s)</math> which can also be factorized as an [[Euler product]], thus leading to the idea of [[Dirichlet character]] defining the exact set of [[Dirichlet series]] having a factorization over the [[prime numbers]].

At least for Re(''s'')&nbsp;≥&nbsp;1:

:<math> \beta(s) = \prod_{p \equiv 1 \ \mathrm{mod} \ 4} \frac{1}{1 - p^{-s}} \prod_{p \equiv 3 \ \mathrm{mod} \ 4} \frac{1}{1 + p^{-s}} </math>

where {{math|1=''p''≡1 mod 4}} are the primes of the form {{math|1=4''n''+1}} (5,13,17,...) and {{math|1=''p''≡3 mod 4}} are the primes of the form {{math|1=4''n''+3}} (3,7,11,...). This can be written compactly as

:<math>\beta(s) = \prod_{p>2\atop p \text{ prime}} \frac{1}{1 -\, \scriptstyle(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}} \textstyle p^{-s}}.</math>

==Functional equation==
The [[functional equation (L-function)|functional equation]] extends the beta function to the left side of the [[complex plane]] Re(''s'') ≤ 0. It is given by
:<math>\beta(1-s)=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{-s}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}s\right)\Gamma(s)\beta(s)</math>
where <math> \Gamma(s)
</math> is the [[gamma function]]. It was conjectured by [[Leonhard Euler|Euler]] in 1749 and proved by [[Carl Johan Malmsten|Malmsten]] in 1842.<ref name=":1" />

==Specific values==
===Positive integers===
For every odd positive integer <math>2n+1</math>, the following equation holds:<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Dirichlet Beta Function |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2024-08-08 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
:<math>\beta(2n+1)\;=\;\frac{(-1)^n E_{2n}}{2(2n)!}\left(\frac\pi2\right)^{2n+1}</math>
where <math>E_n</math> is the n-th [[Euler numbers|Euler Number]]. This yields:

:<math>\beta(1)\;=\;\frac{\pi}{4}, </math>
:<math>\beta(3)\;=\;\frac{\pi^3}{32},</math>
:<math>\beta(5)\;=\;\frac{5\pi^5}{1536},</math>
:<math>\beta(7)\;=\;\frac{61\pi^7}{184320}</math>
For the values of the Dirichlet beta function at even positive integers no elementary closed form is known, and no method has yet been found for determining the arithmetic nature of even beta values (similarly to the Riemann zeta function at odd integers greater than 3). The number <math>\beta(2)=G</math> is known as [[Catalan's constant]].

It has been proven that infinitely many numbers of the form <math>\beta(2n)</math><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rivoal |first1=T. |last2=Zudilin |first2=W. |date=2003 |title=Diophantine properties of numbers related to Catalan's constant |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00208-003-0420-2 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |language=en |volume=326 |issue=4 |pages=705–721 |doi=10.1007/s00208-003-0420-2 |issn=1432-1807|hdl=1959.13/803688 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and at least one of the numbers <math>\beta(2), \beta(4), \beta(6), ..., \beta(12)</math> are irrational.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zudilin |first=Wadim |date=2019 |title=Arithmetic of Catalan's constant and its relatives |journal=Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg |volume=89 |issue=1 |pages=45–53 |doi=10.1007/s12188-019-00203-w |issn=0025-5858|doi-access=free |arxiv=1804.09922 }}</ref>

The even beta values may be given in terms of the [[Polygamma function|polygamma functions]] and the [[Bernoulli numbers]]:<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kölbig |first=K. S. |date=1996 |title=The polygamma function ψ(k)(x) for x=14 and x=34 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0377042796000556 |journal=Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics |volume=75 |issue=1 |pages=43–46 |doi=10.1016/S0377-0427(96)00055-6 |issn=0377-0427|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

:<math>
\beta(2n)=\frac{\psi^{(2n-1)}(1/4)}{4^{2n-1}(2n)!}n - \frac{\pi^{2n}(2^{2n}-1)|B_{2n}|}{2(2n)!}
</math> 
We can also express the beta function for positive <math>n</math> in terms of the [[inverse tangent integral]]:
:<math>\beta(n)=\text{Ti}_n(1)</math>
:<math>\beta(1)=\arctan(1)</math>

For every positive integer ''k'':{{citation needed|date=September 2016}}
:<math>\beta(2k)=\frac{1}{2(2k-1)!}\sum_{m=0}^\infty\left(\left(\sum_{l=0}^{k-1}\binom{2k-1}{2l}\frac{(-1)^{l}A_{2k-2l-1}}{2l+2m+1}\right)-\frac{(-1)^{k-1}}{2m+2k}\right)\frac{A_{2m}}{(2m)!}{\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}^{2m+2k},</math>
where <math>A_{k}</math> is the [[Euler zigzag number]].

===Negative integers===
For negative odd integers, the function is zero:
:<math>\beta(-2n-1)\;=\;0</math>
For every negative even integer it holds:<ref name=":0" />
:<math>\beta(-2n)\;=\;\frac12E_{2n}</math>.
It further is:
:<math>\beta(0)\;=\; \frac{1}{2} </math>.

===Derivative===
We have:<ref name=":0" />

<math>\beta'(-1)=\frac{2G}\pi</math>

<math>\beta'(0)=2\ln\Gamma(\tfrac14)-\ln\pi-\tfrac32\ln2=\ln\tfrac\varpi{\sqrt\pi}</math>

<math>\beta'(1)=\tfrac\pi4(\gamma+2\ln2+3\ln\pi-4\ln\Gamma(\tfrac14))=\tfrac\pi4(\gamma-\ln2+2\ln\tfrac\pi\varpi)</math>

with <math> \gamma
</math> being [[Euler's constant]], <math> \varpi
</math> being the [[Lemniscate constant]] and <math> G
</math> being [[Catalan's constant]]. The last identity was derived by [[Carl Johan Malmsten|Malmsten]] in 1842.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Blagouchine |first=Iaroslav V. |date=2014-10-01 |title=Rediscovery of Malmsten's integrals, their evaluation by contour integration methods and some related results |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11139-013-9528-5 |journal=The Ramanujan Journal |language=en |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=21–110 |doi=10.1007/s11139-013-9528-5 |issn=1572-9303|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
